newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa money mkt jump temporary, traders upbeat.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa money mkt jump temporary, traders upbeat.

text.p: A close to one billion rand jump in the daily money market shortage on Monday was a temporary blip and the bullish short- to medium-term scenario remained intact, money market traders said.
They attributed the sharp rise to a lack of expected government expenditure flowing into the market, noting that there had been no major outflows.

South Africa's money market shortage jumped to 10.370 billion rand on Monday from 9.556 billion rand on Saturday, the Reserve Bank said. It stood at 9.563 billion rand on Friday and 8.732 billion rand on Thursday after rising to a worst level of around 11.3 billion rand over the Christmas period.
But leading banks kept their short-term rates unchanged with three-month NCD rates between 17.30 and 17.50 percent and the 90-day BA rate between 16.65 and 16.85 percent.

At the long end of the market the yield on the the R150 bond had last retraced to 15.83 percent from 15.73 percent at the opening and 15.78 at 1400 GMT on Monday as investors took fright after South Africa rejected a U.S. threat over its planned sale of arms to Syria.
Traders said the jump in the shortage had filtered through to shorter-dated bonds earlier in the day but the effect was minor and seen short-term.

"Apparently it was an expectation of government expenditure over the last couple of days that did not come through...but it will be coming through hopefully by the end of the week and the shortage is perceived to be going back down," a trader at one of the leading banks said.
"There's a bit of churning going on before we carry on down," he added.
The bullish sentiment was seen continuing, supported by positive fundamentals.

One trader commented: "There's a lot of positive sentiment, foreign interest. We've seen big orders in the bonds, the rand is holding up very strongly, call rates are lower ...so it's looking strong."
Call rates have come down from a high of 18.25 percent to 17.00 percent over the last week and a half.
One chief trader said he was optimistic about the coming months and believed rates could come down further, paving the way for a bank rate cut in the first half of the year.
"We are very positive about the coming weeks and months feeling that the rates could come down further...we might have a bank rate cut not now but at least in the first half of the year," he said.
